answer: Glacier cadence lock: an identity's request inter-arrival times must follow a slow-ramping envelope, starting near-zero traffic and rising to a per-account zenith over days, with no burst above the fitted curve. New identities cannot front-load work. Each one must sustain low-rate traffic through the warmup, and sybils must pay that wall-clock delay plus idle connection costs for every clone, since parallel identities each wait out the same slow ramp. Timber-shaped traffic (steady growth, no spikes) is the only accepted pattern.
